intro: A rollout can contain several episodes or stop before an episode ends. Follow how future rewards contribute, and where a terminal transition must cut that contribution.
task: Compute reward-to-go at every transition. Change one terminal flag and predict which earlier returns change before running the examples.
requirements: rewards and terminated are equal-length vectors. terminated contains numeric 0 or 1; 1 marks a true terminal transition. discount is a scalar in [0,1], and bootstrap is the value after the final transition.
Starting with running=bootstrap, visit t from last to first and set running=rewards[t]+discount*(1-terminated[t])*running. Return all running values as a NumPy vector in original time order.
A true terminal transition removes its bootstrap and every later reward. A nonterminal rollout cutoff retains bootstrap. Time-limit truncation should be supplied as 0 when it should bootstrap.

Use real finite numeric inputs of magnitude at most 1e30, excluding boolean parameters. Vectors have 1..256 entries and each matrix axis has length 1..256 unless a stricter bound is stated. Leave caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Walk backward
hints.body: At time t the accumulated suffix already represents the return beginning at t+1.

hints.title: Separate terminal from cutoff
hints.body: The terminal flag belongs to the transition producing rewards[t], so apply it to the future term only.

explanation: The backward recurrence is equivalent to a discounted sum of future rewards up to a terminal boundary, plus a discounted bootstrap if the rollout ends first.
Rewards from a later episode cannot cross a terminal transition. A collected rollout ending is not itself proof that the environment terminated.
